generatedProse.practice-connection:
From here, integrity is something you practise in every piece of academic work. Each source you reference with purpose, each judgement about quoting or paraphrasing, each difficult case you handle by the values, is integrity owned rather than obeyed. The habit to keep is simple: use your sources with judgement, and let the values decide the hard calls.

That same habit carries into professional life. Wherever you are trusted with the truth, and your account of where knowledge came from has to be relied on, the people who are trusted are the ones who earned it by owning it. The integrity you have just learned to defend is one you will use long after you graduate.
